title: Drug-controlled CAR-T cells through the regulation of cell-cell interactions
authors: Scheller L; Attianese GMPG; Castellanos-Rueda R; Di Roberto RB; Barden M; Riboulet M; Shui S; Cribioli E; Marchand A; Georgeon S; Abken H; Reddy S; Correia B; Irving M
one_liner_zh: 该文研究药物调控CAR-T细胞间相互作用，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合，与课题无关。
abstract: CAR T-cell therapy is constrained by on-target, off-tumor toxicities as well as cellular exhaustion due to chronic antigen exposure. CARs comprising small-molecule controlled switches can enhance both safety and therapeutic efficacy but are limited by the scarcity of non-immunogenic protein elements responsive to non-immunosuppressive, clinically approved drugs with favorable pharmacodynamics. Here, we combine rational design and library-based optimization of a protein-protein interaction (PPI) of human origin to develop venetoclax-controlled Drug-Regulated Off-switch PPI (DROP)-CARs. DROP-CARs enable dose-dependent release of the tumor-targeting scFv and consequent T-cell dissociation from the target tumor cell. Additionally, we present proof-of-concept for a dual DROP-CAR controlled by different small molecules, as well as for logic-gated synthetic receptors enabling logic-gated STAT3 signaling. We demonstrate in vitro and in vivo function of DROP-CAR T cells and conclude that the approach holds important promise for clinical application.
abstract_zh: CAR T细胞疗法受到靶向肿瘤外毒性以及慢性抗原暴露导致的细胞耗竭的制约。包含小分子控制开关的CAR能够增强安全性和治疗效果，但受限于缺乏对非免疫抑制、临床批准且具有良好药代动力学特性的药物有响应的人源非免疫原性蛋白元件。在此，我们结合理性设计和对人源蛋白-蛋白相互作用（PPI）的文库优化，开发了维奈克拉控制的药物调控关闭开关PPI（DROP）-CAR。DROP-CAR能够实现剂量依赖性的肿瘤靶向scFv释放，进而使T细胞与靶肿瘤细胞解离。此外，我们展示了由不同小分子控制的双DROP-CAR的概念验证，以及实现逻辑门控STAT3信号传导的逻辑门控合成受体。我们在体外和体内证明了DROP-CAR T细胞的功能，并得出结论，该方法对临床应用具有重要前景。
